subject: maths
title: Power of a power and the zero index

scenes.heading: Power of a power and the zero index
scenes.say: What is seven to the power of zero? Most people guess zero, but the answer is one. In this video you'll see why, and how to raise a power to another power.
scenes.caption: What is 7⁰? Most people guess 0, but the answer is 1. In this video you'll see why, and how to raise a power to another power.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Eggs in cartons, cartons in boxes, boxes in crates: multiply the groups
scenes.breaks: The zero index has no egg picture: a crate of zero boxes holds 0 eggs, but x⁰ = 1.
scenes.say: Eggs come in cartons, cartons go in boxes, and boxes go in crates. To count the eggs, you multiply the groups. A power of a power works the same way. x cubed, all to the power of four, is four groups of three x's. That's twelve x's, so x to the twelfth.
scenes.caption: Eggs come in cartons, cartons go in boxes, and boxes go in crates. To count the eggs, you multiply the groups. A power of a power works the same way. (x³)⁴ is 4 groups of 3 x's. That's 12 x's, so x¹².

scenes.heading: Third index law
scenes.say: The third index law: a to the m, all to the power of n, equals a to the m times n. For a power of a power, multiply the indices. Check: two cubed, squared, is eight squared, which is sixty-four. And two to the sixth is also sixty-four.
scenes.caption: The third index law: (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐˣⁿ. For a power of a power, multiply the indices. Check: (2³)² = 8² = 64. And 2⁶ is also 64.

scenes.heading: Everything in the bracket
scenes.question: Simplify (2m³n)⁴.
scenes.say: The power outside a bracket applies to everything inside. Simplify two m cubed n, all to the power of four. Two to the fourth is sixteen, not eight. m cubed to the fourth is m to the twelfth. n to the fourth stays n to the fourth. The answer is sixteen m to the twelfth, n to the fourth.
scenes.caption: The power outside a bracket applies to everything inside. Simplify (2m³n)⁴. 2⁴ = 16, not 8. (m³)⁴ = m¹². (n)⁴ = n⁴. The answer is 16m¹²n⁴.

scenes.heading: Why a⁰ = 1
scenes.say: Now the zero index. Two cubed is eight, two squared is four, two to the one is two. Each step down halves the value, so two to the zero is one. Or think of x to the fifth divided by x to the fifth: subtracting the indices gives x to the zero, but anything divided by itself is one.
scenes.caption: Now the zero index. 2³ = 8, 2² = 4, 2¹ = 2. Each step down halves the value, so 2⁰ = 1. Or think of x⁵ ÷ x⁵: subtracting the indices gives x⁰, but anything divided by itself is 1.

scenes.heading: Watch the coefficient
scenes.say: Be careful with coefficients. In five x to the zero, only the x is raised to zero, so it's five times one, which is five. But in bracket five x, to the zero, the whole bracket is raised to zero, so it's one.
scenes.caption: Be careful with coefficients. In 5x⁰, only the x is raised to 0, so it's 5 × 1 = 5. But in (5x)⁰, the whole bracket is raised to 0, so it's 1.

points: Power of a power: multiply the indices
Every factor in the bracket gets the power
Brackets first, then multiply or divide
scenes.say: Quick recap. For a power of a power, multiply the indices. The power outside a bracket goes to every factor inside. Anything except zero, to the power zero, is one. And watch which part the zero is attached to. Now try the practice questions!
